hooks.text: A visible star vanished by choking on its own dust.
How did one of our galaxy's largest stars vanish from human sight?
A monster star once visible to human eyes choked itself dark.

title: The Monster Star That Choked Itself Dark
description: VY Canis Majoris was once visible to human eyes before choking on its own ejected dust. Here is how one of our galaxy's largest hypergiants hid from sight.

beats.text: A visible star vanished by choking on its own dust.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope view of the nebula surrounding VY Canis Majoris, 2007
queries: VY Canis Majoris Hubble Space Telescope

beats.text: In 1801, skywatchers logged the red hypergiant VY [Canis](/kˈAnˈɪs/) Majoris as a bright naked-eye light.
beats.visual: Wide-field photograph of constellation Canis Major in the night sky, 2011

beats.text: Located 3,900 light-years away, this behemoth sits among the largest stars in the Milky Way.
beats.visual: Infrared view of interstellar molecular cloud Sh 2-310, 2015

beats.text: If placed in our solar system, its radius—1,420 times our Sun's—would swallow Jupiter.
beats.visual: Scale diagram comparing the radius of VY Canis Majoris to Jupiter's orbit, 2021
queries: Star size comparison VY Canis Majoris
VY Canis Majoris size comparison Sun Jupiter

beats.text: Boiling convection cells larger than our entire Sun violently belch hot gas into space.
beats.visual: Artist illustration of giant boiling convection cells on a red hypergiant star, 2021

beats.text: That ejected gas cools into dense clouds holding complex molecules like water and carbon monoxide.
beats.visual: VLT SPHERE coronagraphic image showing ejected dust knots around VY Canis Majoris, 2015

beats.text: Instead of exploding as a supernova, scientists theorize this titan could collapse directly into a black hole.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a massive star collapsing directly into a black hole, 2020
queries: Stellar black hole artist concept NASA

beats.text: That thick shroud erased a naked-eye beacon, leaving only telescopes to track the monster.
beats.visual: Very Large Telescope array at Cerro Paranal pointing toward the night sky, 2019

better_than_last: Elevated narrative payoff by introducing water/carbon monoxide molecule formation and direct black hole collapse details, avoiding standard star scale tropes.
